name: Host card emulation (HCE)
plain: Lets an app act as a contactless card or key that other readers tap.
meaning: A phone that emulates a card can hold payment, transit or access credentials without the OS wallet. Opening it to apps changes who controls tap to pay.

android.prompt_ui: User picks default payment app in Settings > Tap & pay
android.revocation: Settings > Connected devices > NFC > Contactless payments
android.store_policy: Play: payments apps follow Payments policy
android.note: Android 10 can set the default in Settings; offhost secure element supported.

ios.prompt_ui: Apple Pay stays default outside the EU; EU users can choose
ios.store_policy: Entitlement limited to developers in the EEA, with a licensing agreement
ios.note: EEA only at first; iOS 18.1 adds the NFC and SE platform outside the EU for some countries; scope for 2026 should be re-checked.

limits.headline: Can act as a contactless card or key when you pick it as default
limits.user_action: You choose the app in Settings under Tap and pay, then tap a reader
can: Answer readers with a stored card, ticket or key
Hold payment, transit or access credentials without the system wallet
Run on Android with no Google approval
cannot: Become the default payment app without you choosing it
Work on iPhone without Apple's entitlement
Replace Apple Pay as the default on iPhone outside the EU
limits.differs: Android lets any app do this since 2013; iPhone began in the EU and reached some other countries from iOS 18.1.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app act as a contactless card or key that readers can tap.

marketing.name: Host card emulation
marketing.pitch: Let your app act as a contactless card, such as a payment or transit card, without special hardware.

story.for_you: You hold your phone to a reader and the door opens or the bus lets you on. The app does this without the Wallet app opening. You can set which app answers in Settings.
story.for_makers: A company can build a custom tap card for a loyalty scheme, transit or access control and skip the system wallet. It runs in software on Android with no approval. On iPhone it is limited to approved regions and developers.

use_cases.example: A city bus app holds a ticket you can tap at the gate.
An office badge app opens doors when you tap your phone.
A bank app sends a one time code to the shop's reader.
A car sharing app taps the car to unlock.
A student card app opens the library gate.
A loyalty app earns points with a tap at the till.
A hotel app holds a room key that expires after your stay.

story.android_note: Android 10 lets you pick the default tap app in Settings, and it can use the phone's secure chip.
story.ios_note: iPhone first opened this in the EEA. iOS 18.1 added the NFC and secure element platform outside the EU for some countries. Scope for 2026 should be re-checked.

technical_bounds: iOS needs an Apple entitlement, commercial agreement and fees
Android requires the user to pick the default payment app for payments AIDs

history.change: HCE based contactless payments opened to apps in the EEA
NFC and Secure Element platform for in app contactless in several countries
